achievement of agreement on this problem in the -interests of ensuring a lasting and durable peace among all states, the Soviet government is again prepared to make steps forward to meet the western powers and to agree on a different sequence of carrying out disarmament measures, if that sequence is more acceptable to the western powers.
Being an ardent champion of the earliest deliverance of mankind from the threat of a rocket and nuclear war, the Soviet government proposes that agreement be reached to begin the process of general and complete disarmament by the prohibition and destruction under international control at the first stage of all means of carrying nuclear weapons to target with the simultaneous elimination of military bases on foreign territories.
When war missiles of all ranges, air force, submarines and surface naval vessels, artillery capable of firing nuclear shells and all other means of delivering to targets weapons of mass destruction will be eliminated and states will not have armed forces and military installations beyond their national borders, one country's attack against another with atomic and hydrogen weapons will become practically impossible.
Being desirous to reach this goal the Soviet union expresses its willingness to begin disarmament by the destruction of all means of delivering nuclear weapons to targets, notwithstanding its generally recognized superiority in the most modern and effective means of that kind, namely, in intercontinental ballistic missiles.
In this case during the next, second stage of the disarmament program such measures could be carried out as banning nuclear, biological and chemical weapons, destroying all their stocks and terminating their further manufacture. The menace of a nuclear war in whatever form would be removed for good. At the same time a considerable reduction of armed forces and conventional armaments of states would be carried out.
The third stage would mark the completion of general and complete disarmament, the disbanding of all armies, war ministries, general staffs, the abolition of military service and of military training of youth, the complete cessation of appropriating funds for military purposes.
It is proposed that all this disarmament program shall be implemented on the basis of an international treaty in the course of a definite period of time-within four years or during another period agreed upon, and under effective international control.
In the course of discussing the question of general and complete disarmament in international bodies a great deal of attention has
been drawn to the question of measures to be taken for ensuring the peace and maintaining international law and order in the relations between states under the conditions of general and complete disarmament. The Soviet government proposes that the states parties to the treaty would jointly examine this question in detail so that in the course of the implementation of the third and final stage there would be taken necessary measures in accordance with the U.N. charter for the maintenance of peace in the conditions of general and complete disarmament including the obligation by states to place, when necessary, police (militia) detachments at the disposal of the security council to ensure keeping the peace. Naturally, such police (militia) detachments can be used exclusively for the maintenance of peace among nations and not for the suppression of peoples who are struggling for their independence and social progress, and not for the interference in the internal affairs of states.
It is proposed that all disarmament measures be implemented under strict international control from the beginning to the end. For this purpose the parties to the treaty shall set up an international control organization whose scope of competence will include all disarmament measures and will expand as these measures will be assuming still more comprehensive and far-reaching nature.
In accordance with the abovestated the Soviet government submits the draft basic provisions of a treaty on general and complete disarmament.
Basic provisions of a treaty on general and complete disarmament
The governments of the states members of the 10 nation committee on disarmament set up in 1959, being guided by the resolution of the XIV session of the U.N. general assembly of November 20, 1959, "On general and complete disarmament", in the interests of saying mankind from the threat of a new war and in the interests of securing stable and inviolable peace on earth recognize it necessary to proceed without delay to the practical solution of the task of general and complete disarmament, and have resolved to this end to work out a treaty on general and complete disarmament, which will include the following basic provisions:
I.	General and complete disarmament envisages:
-the disbanding of all armed forces of states and the prohibition of their re-establishment in any form whatever;
-the prohibition and the destruction of all stockpiles of and the cessation of the manufacture of all kinds of armaments, including

atomic, hydrogen, chemicals, bacteriological and other types of weapons of mass destruction;
-the destruction of all means for delivering the weapons of mass destruction to targets;
-the liquidation of all kinds of military bases, the withdrawal and the disbanding of all foreign troops stationed in the territory of any states;
-the abolition of all kinds of military services of citizens;
-the termination of military training of the population and the abolition of all military educational institutions;
-the abolition of war ministries, general staffs and their local agencies, as well as of all other military and paramilitary establishments and organizations;
-the discontinuance of the appropriation of funds for military purposes whether from state budgets or from public organizations and private individuals.
After the completion of general and complete disarmament states shall retain at their disposal only strictly limited contingents of police (militia), the size of which shall be agreed upon for each country and which shall be equipped with small firearms and intended for the maintenance of internal order and the protection of personal security of citizens.
II.	General and complete disarmament shall be implemented by all states at one and the same strictly defined time which shall be agreed upon; and the disarmament process shall be carried out gradually, by three consecutive stages, having in mind that at no stage a state shall obtain military advantages, flowing from the course of disarmament, over other states.
For the consideration of the question of other states joining the agreement on general and complete disarmament a conference shall be held with all countries participating.
III.	All disarmament measures from the beginning to the end shall be carried out under strict and effective international control, that is:
(a)	immediately after the signing of the treaty a preparatory commission shall be set up, whose task will be to implement practical measures for establishing an international organization of control over general and complete disarmament;
(b)	a control organization shall be set up within the framework of the United Nations on the treaty coming into force.
It shall consist of all states, parties to the treaty, and their representatives shall meet periodically for conferences to consider questions related to the carrying out of effective control over disarmament. The conference shall elect a control council, consisting of permanent and non-permanent members,
which shall have its own local agencies. The control council shall consist of the representatives of socialist countries, the representatives of states that participate now in the western military and political alliances, and the representatives of neutral countries. Barring cases specially agreed upon, decisions in the control council shall be taken by the two third majority of votes on the questions of essence and on the questions of procedure -by a simple majority of votes.
(c)	The control council shall effect practical guidance of the control system, work out instructions as well as make timely analysis and processing of reports it shall receive. States shall submit the information on their armed forces and armaments to the control council.
(d)	The control organization shall have in all countries parties to the agreement its own personnel, recruited on the international basis with the principle of just geographical distribution taken into consideration, and in accordance with the provisions of the treaty. The control organization shall place its inspectors on the territories of states in such a way as to enable them to start exercising their functions the moment states begin the implementation of measures in the field of disarmament. Each party to the treaty shall undertake to ensure timely and unrestricted access to inspectors and inspection teams within its territory to any point where disarmament measures to be verified will be effected, or to any area where on the spot inspection of such measures will be carried out. With this purpose parties to the treaty shall at the expense of the control organization make all necessary means of transportation available to the personnel of the control organization for travelling within their territory.
(e)	The control organization personnel shall enjoy on the territory of each party to the treaty such privileges and immunity that are necessary for independent and unrestricted implementation of control over the fulfillment of the disarmament treaty.
(f)	All expenditures of the international control organization shall be covered at the expense of the states parties to the treaty. The scale of the contributions of states shall be fixed in the text of the treaty on general and complete disarmament.
The control organization shall at each stage have powers with regard to the scope and nature of measures in the field of disarmament.
The basic measures in the disarmament field are distributed by three stages of the program of general and complete disarmament in the following way:

The first stage
1.	All means of delivering nuclear weapons shall be removed from the armed forces of states and destroyed; their manufacture shall be stopped. It includes:
-strategic and tactical missiles, pilotless planes of all types, all military aircraft capable of delivering nuclear weapon;
-surface naval vessels that can be used as carriers of nuclear weapon;
-submarines of all classes and types;
-all artillery systems as well as other means that can be used as carriers of atomic and hydrogen weapon.
2.	All foreign troops shall be withdrawn from alien territories to within their national frontiers. Foreign military bases and depots of all kinds, both relinquished after the withdrawal of troops and alternate ones, shall be abolished.
3.	From the very beginning of the first stage and until after the final destruction of all means of delivering nuclear weapons the putting into orbit or the placing in outer space of special devices, the crossing by naval vessels of the limits of their territorial waters and the flights beyond their national territory by military aircraft, capable of carrying weapons of mass destruction shall be prohibited.
4.	The launching of rockets shall be carried out solely for peaceful purposes and in accordance with predetermined and mutually agreed criteria and shall be accompanied by agreed measures of verification including the inspection on the sites of launching such rockets.
5.	States having at their disposal nuclear weapons shall undertake not to transfer such weapons or information necessary for the manufacture thereof to the states which do not possess such weapons. At the same time the states possessing no nuclear weapons shall undertake to refrain from the manufacture of such weapons.
6.	Accordingly states shall reduce their military expenditures.
7.	The following control measures shall be carried out at the first stage:
On the spot international control shall be established over the destruction of rocket weapons, military aircraft, surface naval vessels, submarines and other means which could be used as carriers of atomic and hydrogen weapons.
International inspection teams shall be dispatched to the places of deployment of military bases and troops on foreign territories to supervise the elimination of the said bases and the withdrawal of military personnel and
troops to within their own national territories, control shall be also established on airfields and at ports to ensure these airfields and ports not being used for military purposes. At the same time the destruction of missile launching sites shall be carried out under the supervision of an international control organization with the exception to the sites which will be maintained for the launching of rockets for peaceful purposes.
The control organization will be entitled to unrestricted inspection of all enterprises, plants, factories and shipyards which were previously engaged fully or in part in the production of missiles, aircraft, surface naval vessels, submarines and all other means of delivering nuclear weapons to prevent clandestine production of armaments which could be used as carriers of atomic and hydrogen weapons. On agreement fixed control teams may be established at some works and in-tallations.
International inspection teams dispatched by the control organization shall be entitled to carry out comprehensive examination of rocket devices, being launched for peaceful purposes and to be present at the time of launching.
The inspectors shall communicate with the control council through existing channels of communication and there shall be provided such privileges which will ensure prompt delivery of reports and instructions.
8.	At the first stage joint studies shall be undertaken of the measures on the discontinuance of the manufacture of nuclear, chemical and bacteriological weapons and on the destruction of the stockpiles of such types of weapons, i.e. of the measures which are to be implemented at the second stage.
9.	The first stage must be accomplished within 1-1.5 years. The international control organization shall review the results of carrying out the measures of the first stage to report on them to the states parties to the treaty as well as to the security council and U.N. general assembly.
The second stage
1.	There shall be a complete prohibition of nuclear, chemical, bacteriological and other weapons of mass destruction along with the cessation of the manufacture and the destruction of all the stockpiles thereof.
2.	The armed forces of all states shall be reduced to agreed levels, the armed forces level for the U.S.A. and the U.S.S.R. shall not exceed 1.7 million men. Conventional weapons and ammunitions thus released shall be destroyed and military equipment shall be either

destroyed or be used for peaceful purposes. Military expenditures of states shall be reduced accordingly.
3.	The following measures of control shall be undertaken at the second stage:
Representatives of the control organization shall make on the spot inspection of the destruction of all available stockpiles of nuclear, chemical and bacteriological weapons. The control organization shall be entitled to inspect all enterprises engaged in the extraction of atomic raw materials, in the production or use of atomic materials and atomic energy. Fixed control teams may be established, subject to agreement, at some enterprises and installations.
On the spot international control shall be established to supervise the disbandment of troops and the destruction of armament.
Inspectors shall:
Supervise the exact and timely compliance with the decisions on the disbandment of military formations and units, elimination and destruction of material of conventional arms, military equipment and ammunition; report to the control council and to the government of the host country.
International inspection groups shall include experts depending on the nature of units subject to disbandment and the types of weapons to be destroyed.
The control organization shall have unrestricted access to the documents pertaining to budget allocations of states for military purposes including all the decrees of legislative and executive bodies on this subject.
4.	Joint studies shall be undertaken at the second stage of the following measures to be implemented at the third stage;
(a)	measures to assure compliance with the treaty on general and complete disarmament upon the implementation of all measures stipulated in such a treaty;
(b)	measures to safeguard peace and security in accordance with the U.N. charter in the conditions of general and complete disarmament.
5.	Similar to the transition from the first to the second stage, the international control organization shall sum up the results of the second stage steps to report them to the states parties to the treaty as well as to the security council and the general assembly of the United Nations
The third stage
1.	The elimination of the armed forces of all states shall be completed. States shall retain at their disposal only strictly limited contingents of police (militia) the size of 79951-0-312
which shall be agreed upon for each country and which shall be equipped with small firearms and be intended for the maintenance of internal order and the protection of personal security of citizens.
2.	All remaining types of conventional armaments and ammunitions both in the armed forces and in depots shall be destroyed and the military equipment shall be subject to destruction or use for peaceful purposes.
3.	Military production at all factories shall be terminated including the manufacture of conventional armaments with the exception of the strictly limited manufacture of small firearms designed for the contingents of police (militia) retained by states after the completion of the program of general and complete disarmament.
4.	War ministries, general staffs and all military and paramilitary establishments and organizations shall be abolished. All military training of reservists shall be terminated. In accordance with their respective constitutional procedures, states shall enact legislation prohibiting military education of young people and abolishing military service in all its forms.
5.	The appropriation of funds for military purposes in any form, whether from state bodies and private individuals and public organizations, shall be discontinued. The funds released as a result of the implementation of general and complete disarmament shall be used to reduce or abolish taxation of the population, to subsidize national economies and to furnish economic and technical assistance to underdeveloped countries.
6.	At the third stage the following additional measures on control shall be undertaken:
The international control organization shall send controllers for on the spot inspection of the abolition of war ministries, general staffs, all military and paramilitary establishments and organizations, and of the termination of military training and all other kinds of military activities.
Control shall be established over the discontinuance of the appropriation of funds for military purposes.
The control organization may, when necessary, institute a system of aerial observation and aerial photography over the territories of states.
7.	After the implementation of the program of general and complete disarmament the control organization shall be preserved and shall carry out constant supervision over the implementation by states of the obligations assumed. The control council shall have

the right to send mobile inspection teams to any point or any establishment in the territories of states.
States shall furnish to the control organization data concerning the places of deployment of the contingents of police (militia), their strength in every place (area) as well as any transfer of sizeable contingents of police (militia) near state boundaries. International inspection teams shall carry out comprehensive control so that the strength of police (militia), and their armaments be in conformity with norms agreed upon for each country.
8.	Other measures worked out to assure compliance with the treaty on complete disarmament shall enter into force.
9.	Measures for preserving peace and security in accordance with the UN charter shall be implemented. States shall undertake to place, when necessary, at the disposal of the security council formations out of the contingents of police (militia) remaining at the disposal of states.
Gradually with the implementation of the program of disarmament and the reduction of military expenditures of states the funds thus released as a result of this shall be partly used to render economic assistance to underdeveloped countries.
This is the proposal of the Soviet union concerning the order of the implementation of general and complete disarmament with considerations expressed by the western powers taken into account.
Submitting this proposal the Soviet government expresses its readiness to reach agreement on the implementation of disarmament on the basis of the present proposals constituting an elaboration of the program put forward on September 18, 1959. The most important thing is to conclude an agreement and to finally commence general and complete disarmament which is awaited
by the peoples and urged by the United Nations. The Soviet government is prepared to do it without delay, without waste of time, and it expresses its sincere hope that other states will do likewise being fully conscious of the responsibility for disarmament which rests upon the governments of all states, particularly on the governments of great powers.

The texts of the documents published have been sent to the governments of all countries with whom the U.S.S.R. maintains diplomatic relations. The text of the proposals of the Soviet government on the basic provisions of a treaty on general and complete disarmament has also been sent to the governments of other states.
OTTAWA, June 6, 1960 Dear Mr. Chairman,
Thank you for your letter of June 2 enclosing a series of proposals on disarmament. The implications of these proposals will require careful study in consultation with other interested governments and in the light of other proposals which have been placed before the 10 nation committee in Geneva.
The government of Canada is now engaged in this process of study and consultation and for this reason I welcome your decision formally to present the proposals in the 10 nation committee where they can be the subject of discussion and clarification.
Yours sincerely,
(sgd.) J. G. Diefenbaker Mr. N. S. Khrushchev,
Chairman of the Council of Ministers of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, MOSCOW
